item.title: Clean water, hidden risks: New technology reveals neurotoxicity missed by conventional water quality monitoring
item.description:
Waypoint is curating and commenting on third-party reporting. Original publisher: Phys.org.
Summary: A photograph of an orchestra can tell you whether the musicians are on stage and their instruments are intact. But it cannot tell you whether they are playing in harmony. Even when every musician is present, a subtle loss of coordination can change the entire performance.
Waypoint’s Take: An outdoor reader can treat this as field context — carry one practical craft question into your next outing — light, composition, or subject behavior. Keep the publisher’s claims provisional until you read the original. Dashboard conditions can sit beside this report before you leave.

item.title: A train was delayed by a solar storm. But something didn't add up.
item.description:
Waypoint is curating and commenting on third-party reporting. Original publisher: ScienceDaily.
Summary: Scientists have cracked a 178-year-old mystery surrounding a train delayed by a solar storm, revealing that the famous incident happened in 1848 rather than 1841. The discovery rewrites the early history of space weather and highlights a threat that still endangers modern power grids, satellites, and communication systems.
Waypoint’s Take: Outside, this matters because it can change what you watch for: compare forecast cues with what the sky, wind, and ground feel like before you commit to a route.
